title: Wintering at Carrick: a border fortress town, and an idiosyncratic Bonisagus
notes: Carrick turns out to be a strategic chokepoint disproportionately fortified for its size. Dustin spends the winter soaking up language and culture with Éogan translating; en route they pass a Bonisagus magus whose narrow, idiosyncratic focus on a handful of Arts baffles Dustin.
source: Transcript 2026-07-11 — arrival and settling into Carrick.
body_text:
**Carrick**, though a small town, sits at a geographic **bottleneck** along the northern valley route through Ireland — the natural corridor an English invasion would have to funnel through — and is built up militarily well beyond what its population would otherwise justify. Not because it defends anything valuable in itself, but because whoever holds it can stall an advance.
Interior Ireland reads less like a melting pot and more like a **salad bowl** — communities half a mile apart keeping fiercely distinct dialects, folklore, and even magical idiosyncrasies, without necessarily being hostile to their neighbors. On the way in, the party passes a **Bonisagus magus** who has narrowed his entire practice down to a handful of Arts and Techniques, to the flat exclusion of everything else — a decision that reads as arbitrary rather than tactical, and leaves Dustin quietly baffled.
**Dustin** spends his downtime soaking in language and culture (beyond his tutoring obligations); **Éogan** acts as willing translator and uses the time to get to know **Stijntje** better.

title: Continuing the tribunal prize draft: Falcon's Cliff, and Dagmar's winter reading list
notes: The tribunal prize draft continues asynchronously. The covenant adds Falcon's Cliff to its claimed vis sources, and Dagmar picks two library texts to read over the winter at Oleron — one of them a Mentem summa fit for a Criamon studying Mira/Caris's own tradition.
body_text:
**Vis source claimed: Falcon's Cliff** — a falcon's nest on a coastal cliff not far northwest of the covenant's usual range, where a serpent tries to steal the egg each year. Preventing the theft yields Animal vis; catching the snake after a successful theft yields Vim instead. Flagged as one of the most conveniently reachable options on offer.
**Library texts claimed:** "**The Compact Explained**" (a tractatus on Order of Hermes Lore) and "**The Babble Within Thought**" (a Mentem summa, Level 12 · Quality 11) — the latter picked specifically as a Criamon-relevant text.
**Winter reading plan at Oleron:** Dagmar splits two seasons of study — **The Babble Within Thought** in Fall, and a personal loan from **Caris** (his old Dimicatio-final rival, now something like a mentor-in-residence at Oleron) in Winter.

title: Caris's parting gift: Erroneous Meditations on the Enigma
notes: Caris warms up to Dagmar over the winter, eventually lending him a personal — and, per Caris, worthless — text. A strong Premonitions read reveals it as something else entirely: an extraordinarily detailed account, in diary form, of someone who vanished and came back. The parallel to Solving's own disappearance is not subtle.
source: Transcript 2026-07-11 — Dagmar and Caris at Oleron, 'Erroneous Meditations on the Enigma.'
body_text:
Dagmar spent much of the winter trying — and, for a long stretch, failing — to get Caris to engage socially at all; the Criamon magus ignored him outright for what felt like weeks before finally acknowledging him with a blunt "has the library been suitable for your work?"
Once engaged, Caris proved genuinely willing to talk shop, using an archer's metaphor for the Enigma: aim close and small errors don't matter, but aim at something near the horizon and the same small error becomes miles of drift — and some magi, having only ever aimed close, mistake confidence for precision.
Caris eventually lent Dagmar a personal text, dismissively titled **"Erroneous Meditations on the Enigma"** — his own tone throughout is some version of "I already told you it's worthless, but if it makes you stop asking, fine."
**Dagmar's Premonitions roll came back exceptional.** The text reads like a diary — someone trying to articulate an experience with the logical throughlines missing, the way a dream account never quite holds together. Whatever else it is, it's an **extremely high-resolution single data point** on someone who **disappeared and returned**, trying to describe what happened to them.
Unstated but obvious at the table: this is close kin to the covenant's own defining mystery — **Solving's disappearance into Twilight** in 1220, and the possibility he could still return the same way this account's author apparently did. Dagmar is very interested; this may become his next research thread.

title: The changeling boy: Rody
notes: Passing back through Cruachan, a hedge mage hands Éogan a young Gifted boy to deliver onward, as custom apparently allows. Days into the journey, Éogan works out the boy isn't human at all — and Stijntje independently starts to suspect the same. The party chooses discretion over confrontation, and a real missing child's fate is left to the receiving mages.
source: Transcript 2026-07-11 — 'Rody' the changeling, delivery through Cruachan.
body_text:
On the way back through Cruachan, before Samhain-season traffic, a **hedge mage** approaches Éogan with a young boy in tow and asks outright whether he's a Hermetic magus. On confirming, the hedge mage hands the boy over with no more ceremony than "he's a little late, but he's owed delivery" to the Hermetic covenant near the Hill of Uisneach — and simply trusts that presenting a Hermetic magus with the boy counts as fulfilling the obligation, no receipt required. Éogan accepts him.
**The boy: "Rody," roughly eight and a half.** Talkative, unbothered, and matter-of-fact about his circumstances — his older brother was Gifted too, and was "eaten by goblins" before he could be handed over; Rody was collected a couple of months later as, presumably, the replacement delivery. He's more curious than distressed, and will happily talk anyone's ear off given the chance — including several increasingly creative insults about how badly **Dustin** smells, which read less like genuine complaint and more like Rody converting general unease into something he can weaponize.
Days into the return journey, **Éogan's Fairy Lore roll** (with his usual bonus to social rolls involving fae) catches something off in Rody's sleep — irregular breathing, joints bending the wrong way, an arm folded under him at an angle a human wouldn't hold. **Rody is a changeling.**
Éogan brings this to Dustin privately. Later the same day, unprompted, **Stijntje independently confronts Dustin**: "why are you so concerned about Rody... he's a creature, he's not a boy." Dustin deflects (a successful Communication/Leadership roll) without fully shutting her down — her curiosity is "latent," not resolved.
**The decision:** not force (too risky without an inescapable trap already laid — floated a salt circle as a fallback), not confrontation, not trade for now. The party completes the delivery as tasked, but plans to quietly brief the receiving Hermetic magi on their suspicion, reasoning this isn't their tribunal or their specialty to solve. **Open thread:** the actual Gifted child this changeling replaced is still out there somewhere with the Fae, and nobody the party trusts to find him has been told yet.

title: Dagmar's Falcon's Cliff harvest
notes: Heading north from Oleron, Dagmar stops to harvest the newly claimed Falcon's Cliff vis source — a clean, well-executed capture with a strong yield.
body_text:
En route north from Oleron, Dagmar stops to work the newly claimed **Falcon's Cliff** vis source — timed to the falcon's annual clutch, where a serpent tries to steal the egg each year.
**Method:** an Intellego effect to pinpoint the nest and egg precisely, grogs stationed at range around the site, and **Eyes of the Eagle** to spot the serpent's approach and signal the grogs in time to intercept and capture it alive (uncertain at the time whether the vis-bearing material needed the creature dead or alive — it turned out either the egg or the captured snake could be converted afterward via a bit of magical working).
**Result: a clean success** — a strong "even/odd" roll came up favorably, yielding a hearty six weeks' worth of vis from the harvest.

title: A hidden regio near Carnac
notes: Continuing his coastal survey between Fudarus and Confluensis territory, Dagmar's Eyes of the Eagle roll comes back an outrageous 52 and turns up a low-profile regio in sea caves near Carnac — apparently unnoticed by Carnac itself. He opts to explore it solo with grogs rather than loop the covenant in, expecting to be blamed for something regardless. Cliffhanger for next session.
source: Transcript 2026-07-11 — regio discovery near Carnac, session cliffhanger.
body_text:
Continuing north from the Falcon's Cliff harvest, Dagmar resumes the **regio survey** he'd heard rumors about at the Tribunal, working the stretch of coast **between Fudarus and Confluensis** territory.
**Method:** Eyes of the Eagle (plus an aura bonus) to scan for the tell-tale visual distortion of a regio boundary at long range — deliberately steering wide of Carnac itself along the way, since Dagmar's been avoiding known covenants' territory generally.
**The roll: 52.** Far and away the highest number rolled at this table to date. The result: sea caves under the cliffs near Carnac, giving off a regio signature described as **a mirror-flash rather than a broadcast** — undetectable at normal range, and seemingly unnoticed by Carnac itself, whose own local aura reads as unremarkable. Getting inside means rowing into the caves.
**Decision:** rather than loop Carnac in and risk a diplomatic mess ("I'll just cut to the chase of them blaming us for something"), Dagmar takes a handful of grogs and explores by rowboat alone. **To be continued** — the GM flagged this as something to develop further before the next session.

title: Covenant settles on reachable Aquam/Animal vis sources, passes on the Channel Islands claim
notes: Pre-prize-draft strategizing: stick to coastal resources reachable by ship, don't overextend into unfriendly inland territory, and let Confluensis keep its long-disputed Channel Islands claim as a goodwill chip.
source: Transcript 2026-05-23 — vis-source planning ahead of the prize draft.
body_text:
Before the prize draft, the covenant weighed which vis sources to prioritize if the tribunal went well: **easy access mattered more than the resource type** — trading covers most raw vis needs, but travel through unfriendly or distant territory is a real risk.
GM-offered candidates within easy reach of the covenant's current position: an **Aquam vis source** — sea foam gathered on **St. Martin's Day (November)** at a secluded beach near **Saint-Malo** — and an **Animal vis source** on a cliff along the north shore, near Confluensis's own territory. Both reachable via the English Channel without circling Brittany.
The **Channel Islands vis source** (disputed jurisdiction with the London Tribunal, long held by Confluensis) came up as a possible claim — the covenant chose to **pass on contesting it**, reasoning that Confluensis will simply out-rank them on the pick order anyway, and letting Confluensis keep an already-held resource is a low-cost way to bank goodwill rather than open a jurisdictional fight the covenant doesn't need.

title: First-pick prize draft: Mont-Saint-Michel tide pools, a Terram summa, and Subtle Knives
notes: As tribunal winner, Dagmar leads the pick formally on the covenant's behalf. First vis-source pick and two library picks locked in on the call; remaining picks (20 of 31 prize pawns) to be settled asynchronously with the GM after the session.
source: Transcript 2026-05-23 — prize draft at the closing feast.
body_text:
**Vis-source pick (1st overall pick, uncontested at that slot):** the **Mont-Saint-Michel tide pools** — a high-value, conveniently coastal Aquam source.
**Library picks**, drawn from a partial list the GM shared mid-session and confirmed against the tribunal workbook's library data:
  • **First pick — "De Lapii"**, a rare branch-specific **Terram summa** (Level 17 · Quality 14). Reaction at the table: "that thing's nuts," "I didn't even know books like that existed" — Éogan pushed hardest for this one and it was the clear top priority.
  • **Passed over — "The Primal Power"**, an **Aquam summa** (Level 9 · Quality 17) that came up in the same conversation. High quality, but Éogan's own Aquam score is already **17** — well past the book's level-9 cap — so it would teach him nothing; the party let it go.
  • **Second pick — "Subtle Knives"**, a Penetration summa under Hermetic Theory & Abilities — Éogan's self-described "far second" choice, still locked in for the covenant's library.
**Bookkeeping:** roughly **11 of the covenant's 31 prize pawns** were spent across these first three picks (picks cost one pawn each as the draft cycles through every covenant in placement order); **20 remain** for further rounds, to be resolved asynchronously by the GM after the session as the pick order continues.
